problem: Directly applying 'learning by cheating' (privileged teacher, then student with realistic sensors) to outdoor sidewalk navigation gives a policy that fails when deployed on a real robot. The sim-to-real gap, especially in vision, is large, and public semantic-segmentation networks trained on driving data generalize poorly to sidewalk viewpoints.
motivation: Sidewalk navigation is key for last-mile delivery and neighborhood patrol. Prior outdoor systems need heavy hand engineering or real-world data collection. The paper observes that in simulation more sensors make learning easier, but in the real world each sensor adds its own sim-to-real gap. It therefore ablates sensing modalities in both simulation and the real world.
key_idea: Train a BEV-privileged teacher in a fast abstract world, distill it with DAgger into a student in CARLA that uses pretrained semantic-network intermediate features (not labels or RGB) plus LiDAR and GPS goal, giving zero-shot transfer to a real quadruped on sidewalks.
insight: Feeding the pre-output feature layer of a sidewalk-adapted segmentation net (INF-SEM-FEAT) transfers much better than thresholded semantic labels or raw RGB. Real-world success was 83.3% vs 7.1% for INF-SEM and 25.0% for RGB, even though RGB had a similar simulation validation score (73.16%). Simulation validation alone therefore did not predict real-world transfer, and real-world testing was needed to select the sensors. The last layer discards information, and the features also resist lighting changes.
method: Abstract-world teacher: SAC variant trained in a fast PyBullet world built from OpenStreetMap (Helsinki, ~1 km²) with random obstacles and sidewalk widths of 2-5 m. It uses a privileged 128x128 BEV (3 stacked frames), a 64-ray BEV lidar, and goal direction and distance. Actions are continuous speed and yaw rotation. Reaches 83% validation success.

Student DAgger in CARLA: student cloned in CARLA (7 towns, 14 weathers, 0.6 km²) with L1 action loss against teacher labels. The replay buffer is prefilled with 120k teacher experience pairs, and training takes about 30 h vs more than 300 h from scratch.

Sensing modality selection: ablation over RGB, DEPTH, GT-SEM, INF-SEM, and INF-SEM-FEAT, scored on usefulness, learning difficulty, and sim-to-real sensitivity. Final choice: semantic features (RFEAT 128x60x80), 1D LiDAR (RLID, 272 readings, 6 m cap), and GPS goal direction and distance (RGDD).
Student architecture: pretrained BiSeNetV2 without the last layer as feature extractor, then Network-in-Network, then a 3-layer MLP.

Semantic data augmentation: BiSeNetV2 retrained on Cityscapes (2975 real images) plus GTA (17,535 sidewalk-view and 9,704 road images) and CARLA (6,000 road and 2,400 sidewalk images). The task is reformulated as segmenting the surface the robot currently occupies, which avoids the road-perspective prior.

Localization: phone GPS is used instead of T265 visual odometry, which drifts. The phone is carried by a human walking near the robot because robot vibration degrades GPS. Waypoints switch at a 2 m radius.

setting.backbone: SAC teacher (abstract world, privileged BEV) and a student of BiSeNetV2 features + Network-in-Network + 3-layer MLP, trained by DAgger
setting.training_data: Fully simulated: PyBullet abstract world from OSM Helsinki (teacher); CARLA (7 towns, 14 weathers; student, 120k prefilled teacher pairs); segmentation net trained on Cityscapes 2975 + GTA + CARLA synthetic images (~36k). No real robot data.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (via semantic features), 1-D LiDAR, GPS-derived goal direction/distance
setting.action_space: continuous speed (-10 to 20 cm/step) and yaw rotation (±54°/step)
setting.privileged: none at test time (teacher's BEV is used only in training); GPS via a phone carried by a human operator, and manual human help for road crossing

numbers_note: No standard VLN/ObjectNav benchmark is used. Custom sim validation and real-world evaluations only. Real-world obstacle-course numbers are given in Table I and Fig. 4, with few trials. Long-distance results are reported in Fig. 5 (a figure), and only a few of its numbers appear in the text (3.2 km, 17/19 obstacles avoided, longest uninterrupted stretch 320 m).
results: The INF-SEM-FEAT student reaches 77.90% validation SR in CARLA and 83.3% real-world obstacle-course SR, vs 25.0% for RGB and 7.1% for INF-SEM. It walked 3.2 km of Atlanta sidewalks with limited human interventions and avoided 17 of 19 obstacles. The longest uninterrupted section was 320 m.
limitations: Rule-based waypoint switching is vulnerable to GPS errors and noise; GPS also required a human to carry the phone.
Minor collisions arise from limited sensing and no memory (feed-forward policy), and the robot misclassifies grassy sidewalks and driveways.
Road crossing is done manually by a human operator; evaluation is small-scale, with no baseline comparisons beyond own ablations.
